source_locator: R2297: B.I.33/a, Kutrzeba, 8 September, Pomeranian Cavalry Brigade near Płock
current_activity: Pomeranian Cavalry Brigade is still near Płock on 8 September
notes: Event date: sources covering 1939-09-08, cited below. Kutrzeba (PISM B.I.33/a, R2297) says that in his afternoon conversation with Bortnowski on 8 September 1939, Bortnowski told him that the cavalry brigade had until then stood near Płock and that on 8 September it had telephoned for approval to march behind the Vistula toward the Rembertów area. Kutrzeba took the brigade under his orders and told it not to march behind the Vistula; a Poznań Army courier found it only on 11 September, at a place whose name is not fully preserved in the text layer. The pin is Płock at 10 km for the 8 September position near the town. The requested march to Rembertów is not entered as a completed move. Event definition: A dated headquarters, movement, engagement or withdrawal location in the September 1939 campaign. Event support: PISM B.I.33/a (R2297), the typed after-action account of Gen. Dyw. Tadeusz Kutrzeba, commander of Poznań Army. Memory account, uneven; used at confidence 0.5 unless an independent source agrees. Location and precision are given on the claim row.
